title: Metric Signatures and Trace Lenses — Primer
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc proposes a concise, operational-first format for recording metric semantics ("metric signatures") and a complementary set of trace selection patterns ("trace lenses") so dashboard panels, alerts, and on-call runbooks share unambiguous intent. Target audience: signal owners, dashboard authors, oncall engineers, and SREs supporting inference stacks (hosted, dedicated, private).

Why this matters (short):
- We repeatedly spend time re-interpreting panels during incidents because metric names lack consistent semantics (aggregation window, unit, tag cardinality).
- Traces are noisy; a handful of deterministic lenses lets operators find the causal path faster (eg. cold-kv, cache-miss fanout, model-fallback).
- If metric authors and dashboarders agree on signatures, automated linting and panel templates become possible.

1) Metric signature template (single-line canonical form) — use for every new metric
- name: short snake_case metric id (example: inference.request_p95_ms)
- description: one-sentence human intent
- type: counter | gauge | histogram | summary
- unit: ms | count | bytes | ratio | tokens
- aggregation: instant | 1m_rate | 5m_rate | p90 | p95 | p99 | avg
- cardinality_hint: low | medium | high (helps panel design / indexing)
- useful_tags: comma-separated list (e.g., model, tenant_id, route, region, node_role)
- owner: team or person
- stability: experimental | beta | ga
- cost_impact: low | medium | high (est. query cost sensitivity)

Example (fill):
- name: inference.kv_cache_miss_count
- description: increments when a request results in an LRU/empty hit in per-tenant KV cache
- type: counter
- unit: count
- aggregation: 1m_rate
- cardinality_hint: high
- useful_tags: tenant_id, model, route, region
- owner: eng-serving-runtime
- stability: beta
- cost_impact: medium

Design notes and guidance:
- Prefer explicit aggregation in the signature. If p95 is what systems use for SLOs, record p95 as the aggregation; dashboards can derive other percentiles but the signature is authoritative.
- Unit must be explicit. Never conflate ms and seconds.
- Cardinality_hint drives whether we index or roll up. High-cardinality counters should be pre-aggregated for long-term storage.
- Cost_impact helps dashboard authors choose sampling or materialized views when query budgets are tight.

2) Trace lenses — reusable filters + anchors for rapid investigation
Definition: a trace lens is a short boolean filter + anchor point that extracts a focused set of spans for a common failure mode. Lenses are not full sampling policies; they are investigation recipes attached to panels and runbooks.

Canonical lens fields (one-liners):
- id: lens_name (cold_kv_tail)
- trigger_signal: metric or alert that should point to this lens (eg. kv_cache_miss_count spike)
- span_anchor: span name or operation that defines the investigation root (eg. "kv.read" or "runtime.token_emit")
- matching_predicate: simple filter clauses (status==error, duration>200ms, tags.model==gpt-small, kv.miss==true)
- sample_hint: head | tail | error_only | probabilistic(0.1)
- suggested_view: timeline | flame | top_spans | session_replay
- instrumentation_notes: any required span tags/context to be present

Example lenses (in plain English):
- cold_kv_tail
  - trigger_signal: per-tenant kv_cache_miss_count increase
  - span_anchor: kv.read
  - matching_predicate: kv.hit==false AND duration > 20ms
  - sample_hint: tail
  - suggested_view: timeline + span-stack where node_role==cache_backend

- model_fallback_fanout
  - trigger_signal: model.fallback_rate OR high latency with fallback flag in response
  - span_anchor: router.route_request
  - matching_predicate: routing.fallback==true
  - sample_hint: error_only
  - suggested_view: trace-flame + per-model call ladder (shows upstream fanout)

- batching_backpressure
  - trigger_signal: wall_time_per_batch_ms increase OR batch_queue_length spike
  - span_anchor: batch.dispatch
  - matching_predicate: queue_wait_ms > 50ms AND batch_size < target_size
  - sample_hint: probabilistic(0.2)
  - suggested_view: timeline with annotations for autoscale events

3) Dashboard lens mapping (how panels should reference signatures + lenses)
- Each panel should declare: displayed_metric (canonical name), signature_ref (link or id), lens_refs (0..n lenses), intent_blurb (what this panel is used for).
- Panels solving user-visible SLOs must include a suggested_lens that investigative alerts point to.
- Example panel header template (short):
  Title: Inference p95 (overall)
  displayed_metric: inference.request_p95_ms
  signature_ref: inference.request_p95_ms
  lens_refs: [cold_kv_tail, model_fallback_fanout]
  intent_blurb: customer-observed latency SLO — first checkpoint for routing issues

4) Query and sampling recommendations (practical)
- High-cardinality counters: use 1m rollups and downsampled long-term retention. Keep raw tagged events for 7d, rollups for 90d+.
- Traces for lenses: enable head+error tail for the trigger window +/- 10 minutes. If lens is high-frequency, use probabilistic sampling but keep error-only as full.
- Add computed boolean tags (eg. kv.miss=true) at emit time — much faster to filter in trace backend than to parse payloads later.

5) On-call quick-checklist (first 8 minutes)
- Step 0: read incident title and SLO impact.
- Step 1: open the SLO panel + check p95/p99 across regions and tenants (panel uses inference.request_p95_ms signature).
- Step 2: if latency spike, open suggested_lens -> cold_kv_tail. Are kv misses correlated with tenants?
- Step 3: if trace shows fallback, open model_fallback_fanout lens. Check for sudden routing config changes (link to last canary deploy).
- Step 4: check deployment/infra events (autoscaler, node restarts) and batch queue panels.
- Step 5: escalate to runtime team if model-level latency increases with no kv signal.

6) Dashboard hygiene checklist for signal owners
- Does each panel include signature_ref and intent_blurb?
- Is there at most one panel showing the same canonical aggregation for the same audience? Avoid duplicates with different tag filters.
- Are high-cardinality panels hidden in 'investigation' mode by default?
- Is the panel query annotated with cost_impact and suggested sampling window?

7) Instrumentation changelog and migration notes
- When adding a new metric, create the metric signature doc entry and a trivial dashboard panel stub that references it. Link it in PR description.
- For renames, keep an alias metric for 30 days with bridge queries, update dashboards to new signature_ref, then retire alias.

8) Open questions / trade-offs (for next WG session)
- How aggressively do we want to materialize high-cardinality pre-aggregates vs rely on query-time rollups (cost vs flexibility)?
- Can we automate signature linting in CI for Grafana dashboard PRs? Which fields are strictly required?
- Sampling budget: what global probabilistic baseline should we recommend for traces attached to high-throughput lenses?

9) Immediate TODOs (owner tags)
- Marco: prototype a lint rule that rejects panels without signature_ref (due 2025-12-16).
- Lina: add computed tag kv.miss on cache client instrumentation PR (JIRA-INF-987) and add example trace in github PR 412 (due 2025-12-09).
- Samir: create dashboard template with header metadata and lens links (due 2025-12-12).

Appendix A — quick glossary (short):
- Signature_ref: the single source-of-truth entry describing metric semantics.
- Lens: a reusable trace filter recipe (not a sampling policy).
- Anchor span: the span that identifies the logical root of interest in a trace.

Notes to self (heavier notes / scratch):
- Consider mapping cardinality_hint to retention tiers automatically.
- Think about exporting signature metadata to prometheus_lifecycle endpoints so external teams can discover semantics.
- Slack: #obs-inference has the debate threads; add a periodic digest for signature additions.

End of doc — feedback wanted: Is the signature shape minimal and practical? Are the three lens examples a good initial set?
